claims.claim: The latest assessment puts EU energy-support spending at 17.9 billion euros, with 25 of 27 member states having adopted some form of support in 2026.
claims.episode_span: Twenty-five of the EU’s twenty-seven member states have adopted some form of energy support during 2026, and the latest assessment puts the cost at 17.9 billion euros.
claims.source_title: EU Governments Spend €17.9bn Shielding Consumers from Energy Price Shock
claims.supporting_quote: Twenty-five of the EU’s 27 member states have adopted some form of energy support during 2026, according to the latest assessment of the measures .

claims.claim: More than two-thirds of the energy-support spending directly suppresses prices rather than providing targeted income support.
claims.episode_span: More than two-thirds of the spending directly suppresses energy prices rather than giving targeted income support.
claims.source_title: EU Governments Spend €17.9bn Shielding Consumers from Energy Price Shock
claims.supporting_quote: More than two-thirds of the spending consists of measures that directly suppress energy prices rather than targeted income support.

claims.claim: Measures detailed by 4 May were estimated at 14.5 billion euros, about 0.07 per cent of EU GDP, and extending them through 2026 could cost 38.6 billion euros.

claims.claim: The Commission’s spring assessment found roughly three-quarters of then-current support was not targeted at vulnerable consumers or energy-intensive companies.

claims.claim: Brussels says Europe does not face an immediate security-of-supply problem for winter 2026-27, and the petroleum import bill rose 55.8 per cent in the second quarter while volume rose 1.2 per cent.

claims.claim: An Istanbul court on 30 September blocked T24’s website and social accounts over 118 items, and the site remained blocked after T24 removed them within four hours.
